The root shell is not in the global mount namespace, so Ubuntu\'s mounts would not be visible across sessions. In Magisk, set the mount namespace mode to Global; in KernelSU, use the global namespace in the app profile; in APatch, enable the global namespace.

Mounts Ubuntu at boot and runs, as root, the executable scripts in /etc/uburoot-boot.d inside it, in name order (e.g. 10-sshd that runs /usr/sbin/sshd -p 8022). Scripts should start daemons in the background. Log: /data/local/uburoot/boot.log. Needs the UbuRoot module: install this APK as a module in Magisk, KernelSU or APatch.

UbuRoot requires root with full kernel access: every capability, no seccomp filter and no no_new_privs. Your root manager gave this app less (for example a KernelSU App Profile with fewer capabilities or another SELinux domain). Give UbuRoot the default, unrestricted root profile, then tap Try again.

Checks root, kernel features, hardware, mounts, storage and network, and changes nothing. Attach the report to bug reports. IP addresses, user and host names and serial numbers are hidden unless you include them.
This report includes identifiers. Check it before sharing it.

Root in Ubuntu gets the kernel\'s own interfaces: configfs (USB gadget), debugfs, tracefs, BPF, cgroups, pstore, SELinux, the ROM\'s kernel modules, and uburoot-kernel / uburoot-kmod / uburoot-kbuild. Changes made with them are recorded and undone by Stop all. Applies after Repair mounts.
Give Ubuntu control of the kernel?

With kernel access, root in Ubuntu controls the phone\'s kernel: it can change kernel settings, load modules, switch SELinux, reconfigure USB, and trace everything that runs. A mistake can crash or slow down the phone until it reboots. Changes made with uburoot-kernel are recorded and undone by Stop all, Revert changes or a reboot; changes made by hand (echo into /proc/sys, insmod) are not. Users without sudo get nothing new.
Saved. Kernel access changes on Repair mounts (or after Stop all).
Kernel access is off: turn it on in Settings, then Repair mounts. You can still see the state and revert changes.
Lets root (and only root) read kernel addresses (kptr_restrict = 1), for perf, trace and debugging tools. dmesg and perf already work for root.
Not needed by Ubuntu\'s root: the root manager\'s domain is already unrestricted. It turns SELinux off for every app on the phone.
Turn SELinux off for the whole phone?
Permissive mode removes SELinux protection from EVERY app and service on the phone, not just Ubuntu. Malware gets much easier. It lasts until you switch it back, Revert changes, Stop all or a reboot.
Made with uburoot-kernel / uburoot-kmod, here or inside Ubuntu. Stop all and a reboot undo them too.
Undo every recorded change, newest first: unload the modules loaded through UbuRoot, restore kernel settings and SELinux.
* = loaded through UbuRoot. Load modules inside Ubuntu with sudo uburoot-kmod load FILE.ko; uburoot-kbuild check says what this kernel accepts.

uburoot-hw inside Ubuntu: give users the phone\'s GPU, input, USB, serial and other device groups, take Wi-Fi over from Android, change CPU limits and hold a wake lock. Changes are recorded and undone by Stop all. Applies after Repair mounts.
Give Ubuntu control of the hardware?

With hardware access, root in Ubuntu can hand the phone\'s devices to Ubuntu users, turn Android\'s Wi-Fi off to use the chip itself, change CPU frequencies, take wake locks and open bus nodes. The phone can lose Wi-Fi, drain the battery faster or run hotter until the change is undone. Thermal limits, charger and battery settings stay read-only. Changes made with uburoot-hw are undone by Stop all, Revert changes or a reboot.
Hardware access is off: turn it on in Settings, then Repair mounts. You can still see the state and revert changes.
Grants below are for %1$s, the default user (Settings).
The default user is root, who can use every device already. Pick a user in Settings to grant classes.

Tap a class for its nodes, who uses them and its limits. Routes: direct = the kernel interface is free; bridge = through Android (Phase 3b); takeover = Android stops using it; read = report only. A grant applies to new sessions.
Android keeps Wi-Fi while iw works alongside it. A takeover turns Android\'s Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi scanning off, so wlan0 is Ubuntu\'s: wpa_supplicant, hostapd (access point), scans.
The phone loses its Wi-Fi connection until you give Wi-Fi back, Stop all or reboot. Ubuntu\'s Wi-Fi programs are stopped when it goes back.
Change CPU limits inside Ubuntu: sudo uburoot-hw cpu governor|min|max|online ... (recorded). The phone\'s power service may change them back.
Kernel and hardware changes share one log: this reverts both, as Stop all does.
Undo every recorded kernel and hardware change, newest first: device permissions, CPU settings, wake lock, Wi-Fi takeover, kernel settings, SELinux, modules.
